articles.title: Cameroon Cholera Outbreak: Situation Report #7 (October 6, 2026)
articles.description: Country: Cameroon Source: International Medical Corps Please refer to the attached file. FAST FACTS As of October 5, 459 cholera cases and four deaths had been reported in Minawao Refugee Camp, which currently is home to more than 81,000 refugees and operating at about 325% of intended capacity. Multiple transmission chains are suspected within the camp, where heavy rainfall is increasing the risk of rapid spread among vulnerable populations. Nationwide, according to the most recent government figures, there have been 2,903 confirmed cases and 84 deaths nationwide across 13 health districts. The cholera outbreak in Cameroon has a case fatality rate of 2.89%, which is nearly three times higher than the internationally accepted target of less than 1%. OUR RESPONSE International Medical Corps has been operating in Minawao Refugee Camp since 2013, providing Nigerian refugees with primary, community-based and referred secondary healthcare. In response to the outbreak, our team has treated all 459 patients, expanded the cholera treatment unit to 65 beds, trained 105 health workers in case management and infection prevention, and reached a daily average of 6,478 people through community information sessions on hygiene, safe water and early care-seeking. We are coordinating with national health authorities, United Nations agencies, camp management and humanitarian partners to support a coordinated response.

articles.title: ‘It’s hard to imagine the fires of July’: a bike ride through the Cairngorms in Scotland
articles.description: Wildfires raged through the national park this summer, but much of the landscape remains untouched – and autumn is the perfect time to go In the Cairngorms national park, the bracken is changing from dark green to russet and umber. Birch leaves are lined with gold, while the Scots pines remain proudly green. Autumn is arriving with a little sigh of relief here, after a summer few will forget. The wildfire that began near Glenmore and Abernethy on 15 July burned more than 33 sq km (13 sq miles) of moorland and forest. More than 500 firefighters were involved; homes and businesses were evacuated; and the emergency response lasted over a month. Visiting now, it’s hard to see, or even imagine, the damage. Much of the burned area is high on the hill and far from the roads. It’s a huge loss but, in a national park stretching 4,528 sq km (1,748 sq miles), surprisingly easy to miss. Continue reading...

articles.title: Somali Cash Consortium - Baseline and Endline Findings MPCA Outcomes from the Direct Nutrition Referral Approach: Kismayo & Banadir, Somalia (June 2026)
articles.description: Country: Somalia Source: REACH Initiative Please refer to the attached file. KEY MESSAGES • The use of consumption-based coping strategies declined. The proportion of households with high reduced Coping Strategy Index (rCSI) decreased sharply, from 47% to 2%, while low or medium rCSI increased to 87%. While the proportion of HHs relying on emergency, crisis or stress livelihood coping strategies (LCS) declined, a substantial share continued to rely on these strategies at endline, including 42% using emergency LCS, highlighting continued pressure on livelihoods despite improvements in food consumption. • HH income and expenditures increased, with the largest share spent on food and medical expenses. However, most HHs still relied mainly on casual labour and humanitarian assistance as their primary source of income. Despite this improvement, HHs with debt remained widespread. More than three-quarters of assessed HHs (83%) reported having debt at endline, although the average debt burden declined from USD 84.51 at baseline to USD 70.42 at endline. • Findings indicate that HHs remained highly financially vulnerable, with limited ability to build savings, despite improvements in income and a modest reduction in debt levels. The proportion of HHs with any savings fell sharply from 13% at baseline to just 3% at endline, while average savings declined from USD 3.32 to USD 1.89.
